title: The Ship of Theseus as an Argument Map
production_path_basis: The object states, definitions, motivations, objections, and unresolved tension must remain understandable without narration.
audience: General learners with no philosophy background
assumed_knowledge: arguments can be tested by objections
central_message: The puzzle reveals competing criteria for identity over time rather than proving one official solution.
takeaway: Looking the same is not the same as being numerically one object, and matter, continuity, organization, and causal history can pull judgments apart.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
philosophical_depth: introductory persistence puzzle with numerical/qualitative identity, rival claimants, criteria, and objections
visual_direction: dark conceptual storyboard with procedural planks, balanced claim colors, and explicit reasoning regions
pacing: intuition, gradual change, rival claimant, vocabulary, objections, transfer, synthesis
constraints: give serious criteria equal visual weight
success_criteria: two rival ships are spatially distinct
four criteria each receive support and objection
